title: Molecular and functional characterization of telomeric repeat-containing RNAs in Chinese hamster ovary cells.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the complete Europe PMC supplementary package (6.44 MB). It holds exactly one supplementary file, gkag739_supplemental_file.pdf (5.79 MB), plus the six main-text figure images. I extracted the PDF's embedded text streams (460k characters across ~12 pages, 73 embedded images) and read the legends: they are supplementary figure legends only (Western blots, RNA fluorescence in-situ hybridisation images, foci-per-nucleus quantifications, 'at least 50 nuclei were scored'). No spreadsheet, CSV, TSV or any machine-readable table exists in the package. I also searched the full open-access text (79k characters) for deposited data: zero hits for GEO, GSE, SRA, BioProject, ArrayExpress, Zenodo, figshare, RNA-seq or 'Supplementary Table'.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biology itself (TERRA and ARIA transcripts arise mostly from interstitial telomeric sequences, are polyadenylated, have ~2 h half-lives, and ARIA loss exposes single-stranded DNA) comes from reading the paper; none of it is backed by a downloadable data file. The data availability statement reads in full: 'All data relevant to the study are included in this article or uploaded as the supplementary data.'

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified in the files. The only supplementary item is a 12-page PDF of figures and legends. There is no dataset to download in any machine-readable form, and no accession in any repository (GEO, SRA, BioProject, Zenodo all absent from the text and from NCBI links). The numbers behind every panel exist only as bar charts in images.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no column anywhere. Any prediction target (for example single-stranded-DNA foci count per nucleus, or transcript half-life) would have to be read off printed bar charts by hand, which is construction, not a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No sequences, coordinates or feature table are provided. The Chinese hamster ovary interstitial telomeric sequence locations the paper discusses are not supplied as a BED file or coordinate list; the paper itself notes the CHO genome assembly needs 'further improvement'.

a4_units_stated.note: Not the failure point: units are stated in the figure legends (hours for half-life, foci per nucleus, fold change normalised to total RNA). But they are stated in prose about images, not in any data file.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The experimental unit is a nucleus or a blot lane: legends report 'at least 50 nuclei' or '100 nuclei' per sample across three independent experiments, i.e. hundreds of microscopy observations at most, and none of them are released as rows. Far below the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits a laptop; it is far too small rather than too large.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no file reports a count, so paper, interface and download cannot disagree. Recorded as not-applicable rather than verified agreement.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not the failure point. The measurements are genuine physical assays (RNA fluorescence in-situ hybridisation, dot blot, quantitative PCR), not another model's output. They are simply never released in usable form.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no machine-readable measurements, so no model can be trained or tested on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence around telomere-like repeat tracts to predict how much telomeric repeat RNA is made from each tract.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model the DNA sequence surrounding each interstitial telomeric sequence (a telomere-like TTAGGG repeat tract sitting inside a chromosome rather than at its end) in the Chinese hamster ovary genome. Number of examples: unknown, because no coordinate list or expression table is released.
plain_idea.predict: How much telomeric repeat RNA (TERRA, the G-rich transcript, and ARIA, its C-rich complement) is produced from each tract, and whether losing that RNA exposes single-stranded DNA there. The true answer would come from RNA fluorescence in-situ hybridisation and blot quantifications, which this paper made but published only as figure panels.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Telomere and genome-stability labs would use a map of which repeat tracts are transcribed and which become fragile, since Chinese hamster ovary cells are also the main industrial protein-production cell line and their genome instability costs money. None of that is reachable from this paper's released files.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict per-locus telomeric repeat RNA output (TERRA/ARIA) and single-stranded DNA exposure from flanking genomic sequence in Chinese hamster ovary cells, using a DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer as a frozen backbone. Abandoned because the paper publishes neither the locus coordinates nor any per-locus measurement; both inputs and labels exist only inside figure images.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset; the 6.4 MB figure in working_set_gb is the entire supplementary package I downloaded.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the supplementary files: if the only one is a PDF, there is no dataset. That took one unzip and killed the candidate in under five minutes.

verdict_reason: Pure wet-lab paper with no deposited data: the entire supplement is one PDF of figures and legends, with no table, no accession and no repository entry anywhere in the text. Part A1, A2, A3 and A5 all fail. Even the underlying biology is image-based with roughly 50-100 nuclei per condition, so no amount of extraction effort would reach a modellable number of rows.
